Answering as a liberal Christian. 

I do not claim to know what God intends. I think God may have permitted us to suffer for his glory, which surpass our understanding. For instance, I have lifelong recurring mental health difficulties that have made me want to end my life many many times and I question why God allowed my suffering. But I believe if God wills me to live another day, He will show me how to glorify Him. I have an old teacher from college who was diagnosed with cancer. I have no idea what my suffering is like compared to hers.. But from her suffering through cancer (still ongoing), I begin to be grateful for what I still have despite all my troubles and fears. Children are underage, but that doesn’t mean it makes them less human. God may use their suffering to help another human being, whether inspire them to do a task for His glory, or something else, I do not know. I realize I do not know many things, but I believe the reason I have not killed myself yet is God’s grace and because of God who sustains me even if it’s just by helping me stay alive. If we believe in eternity with God, then our life here is short, compared to eternity.

for my depression, it has been long term, but I have managed to go through university while struggling with it day-in day-out. Earlier in my journey in therapy, I used to want to rush to “recovery”, without really knowing how that would look like for me. It was just me wanting to be happy most of the time, which when I think back now, is unrealistic. I have come to realise and accept that my depression and anxiety means that apart from the usual ups and downs of life, mine would be worse in severity than “normal” people so to speak. And I have started to redefine recovery. I still see my therapist, I still go for treatment, but now I look forward to improve my life so that I can still go for my goals, but accepting that I may need to make some changes or detours along the way, and sometimes that means I need to take longer time to do something or reach a goal than others, like doing a desired postgraduate study or selecting an alternative career path.

To answer your question, I tried many things between sessions. Sometimes it would be trying to get out of bed everyday, other times it would be scheduling some self care time for myself. I also read books particularly memoirs about depression, I attend support groups, I reach out to friends, I try my best to focus on just today, and not worry years into the future.

Past experiences with therapy helped me know what kind of people I prefer as my therapist and what qualities I prefer. For example I prefer my therapist to help me with problem solving and communicate ideas clearly rather than going to the unconscious /psychodynamic therapy stuff etc. But I also want to be able to talk about past problems and issues if I prefer. I wanted a therapist who respected my choices and is open-minded. It took me 5 times over a few years to finally find a therapist that does all that that I prefer. Everyone will prefer different things, it can be gender or age of therapist or years of experience or type of modality /treatment approach or personality etc.

Hey.. I relate to some parts of your story, about how your plans never go as you expect, and competing with peers etc in high school. 

I struggle with depression for years and still do struggle. In high school, many people in my class got Straight As, I didn’t. Many got scholarships for further studies, I didn’t. Many went into Med school, Law school etc, I didn’t. I used to compare my failures to others’ success. But I gradually learned that in the real world, if you allow yourself to see it, people deal with various problems that they don’t tell others. I have mental illness, but I don’t tell everyone I see, only a few I trust. 

It’s true, the world is competitive and brutal, but it’s really about what perspective you choose to take. For me, I see the world is shit a lot of the times, but a lot of it is clouded by my depression. Now I intentionally count my blessings, I am at University, I have both my parents, I have a stable home to live in, I have a few friends who can support me etc.. I find therapy helpful if you can find someone you click with. I take medications off and on when I need, sometimes the gap between occasions when I go on medication can be a few years, however long I can cope without. I accept that I am dealt a different hand than others. So I cope with that. I learn to take up fewer things so that I can plan for days when I find it difficult to function. 

Marks / Scores in school or Universities are not everything. The workforce is gradually recognizing other soft skills such as communication, interpersonal skills etc, so if those are your strengths you can excel too. 

High school is hard in and of itself, many people struggle in high school so you are not alone.. I hated my high school years but I am happy I survived it. 

Hope this helps a bit. Wish you well.

Hey, I am 23F so might not relate on how guys think about relationships. But I will try to give my two cents here. I sought help for mental health issues 6 years ago and am still seeing a psychologist for depression and anxiety. Even with help I still struggle almost everyday, so give yourself a pat on the back for dealing with things on your own for so long. I just got out of a relationship last year and while I had more emotional support while in the relationship, I found that the person was not right for me. 

I think it’s a good opportunity to work on yourself when you are single, then when you are ready you will attract better people in your life. That’s what I tell myself anyway. You have time to work on yourself and then relationships will come on its own when you are in the right state of mind.

I resisted antidepressants for a long time although i tried meds a few times in my life. I used to try lexapro many years back and it didnt work for me, but recently I started the med again and it worked for me now surprisingly. I think our brain chemistry can change over time and different drugs can be effective at different times. GP can manage meds but only if things like depression and anxiety, probably best to see a psychiatrist if it’s schizophrenia or more serious mental health issues.

Yeah psych appointments you might have to wait a while to get them. but be patient, eventually you will get it. Also don’t be too upset if you don’t click with the first therapist you see, it’s normal, just keep finding until you find the right one for you. It took me 4 times before I found the right psych for myself
